database_summary: E‑commerce order dataset (SQLite) with customers, sellers, orders, order line items, payments, product catalog, product category translations, order reviews, and fine-grained geolocation table. Rows represent entities (customers, sellers, products), transactions/events (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews) and descriptive/location lookup (geolocation, product_category_name_translation). Common keys: order_id links orders -> order_items/order_payments/order_reviews; product_id links order_items -> products; seller_id links order_items -> sellers; customer_id links orders -> customers. Geolocation and zip prefixes are many-to-one descriptive lookups by zip code prefix. Schema contains both current state attributes on rows (e.g., orders.order_status) and event/timestamp columns (order timestamps, review timestamps, shipping limits).

accepted.name: orders_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- deterministic parsed ISO timestamps (SQLite stores as TEXT; keep original values too)
  CASE WHEN trim(order_purchase_timestamp) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp_parsed,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_approved_at) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at_parsed,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_carrier_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date_parsed,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_customer_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date_parsed,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_estimated_delivery_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date_parsed
FROM orders
accepted.description: Normalized projection of the orders table with parsed timestamps and preserved identifiers. Use this to join orders to items/payments/reviews and to compute time-based metrics. | Use for: Order lifecycle metrics (time to approve, time to deliver); Filtering orders by status or by presence/absence of timestamps; Joining orders to items/payments/reviews

accepted.name: order_items_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  shipping_limit_date,
  price,
  freight_value,
  CASE WHEN trim(shipping_limit_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE shipping_limit_date END AS shipping_limit_date_parsed
FROM order_items
accepted.description: Projection of order_items preserving item-level identifiers and measures (price, freight) with deterministic casts. Use for item-level aggregations, joins to products and sellers. | Use for: Item-level revenue and freight analysis; Product-level or seller-level sales aggregations; Fulfillment timeliness using shipping_limit_date

accepted.name: order_payments_agg_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_records_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT payment_type) AS payment_types_count
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Aggregate payments per order to get total paid, number of payment records, and distinct payment types. Useful when you need order-level payment totals and payment method variety. | Use for: Reconciling order totals vs payments; Analyzing common payment methods and installment usage; Detecting orders with missing or multiple payment records

accepted.name: order_items_revenue_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(price) AS order_items_price_sum,
  SUM(freight_value) AS order_items_freight_sum,
  COUNT(*) AS order_items_count,
  AVG(price) AS order_items_price_avg
FROM order_items
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Order-level aggregates of item revenue and freight computed from order_items. Use to compute per-order revenue, average item price, and item counts. | Use for: Order revenue calculations; Average item price and item count per order; Comparing payment totals to item totals

accepted.name: orders_with_payments_and_items
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp_parsed AS order_purchase_timestamp,
  pi.order_items_price_sum,
  pi.order_items_freight_sum,
  pi.order_items_count,
  pp.total_payment_value,
  pp.payment_records_count
FROM orders_base o
LEFT JOIN order_items_revenue_by_order pi ON o.order_id = pi.order_id
LEFT JOIN order_payments_agg_by_order pp ON o.order_id = pp.order_id
accepted.description: Denormalized order-level relation joining orders to aggregated payments and aggregated items to produce one row per order with key measures. Useful as a starting point for customer/order-level analysis. | Use for: Order-level profitability and payment completeness; Filtering orders by status while having payment/item metrics; Customer lifetime and order frequency analysis (after further aggregation)

accepted.name: products_with_category_en
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
accepted.description: Product dimension joined to the category translation lookup to expose English category names alongside original category. Use for category-level reporting and joining to order items. | Use for: Aggregating sales by English product category; Filtering products by physical attributes; Joining product attributes to order items for product-level metrics

accepted.name: latest_review_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  review_id,
  order_id,
  review_score,
  review_comment_title,
  review_comment_message,
  review_creation_date,
  review_answer_timestamp
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY review_creation_date DESC, review_id DESC) AS rn
  FROM order_reviews r
) WHERE rn = 1
accepted.description: Selects the most recent review per order by review_creation_date (ties broken by review_id). Useful to get one review row per order when multiple reviews may exist. | Use for: Per-order sentiment or review score analysis; Joining a single review to an order for customer feedback metrics

accepted.name: customer_orders_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS customer_order_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(pi.order_items_price_sum,0)) AS customer_total_items_price,
  SUM(COALESCE(pp.total_payment_value,0)) AS customer_total_payments,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(COALESCE(pi.order_items_price_sum,0)) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) END AS customer_avg_order_items_price
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_items_revenue_by_order pi ON o.order_id = pi.order_id
LEFT JOIN order_payments_agg_by_order pp ON o.order_id = pp.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id
accepted.description: Aggregated order-level metrics rolled up to the customer (customer_id): order count, total order item revenue, total payments, and avg order value. Use for customer lifetime or cohort analyses. | Use for: Customer lifetime value estimates; Identifying high-value customers; Cohort analysis by customer attributes

accepted.name: geolocation_zip_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  MIN(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  MIN(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  COUNT(*) AS geolocation_rows_count,
  MIN(geolocation_city) AS geolocation_city,
  MIN(geolocation_state) AS geolocation_state
FROM geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Aggregate geo lookup to one representative lat/lng per geolocation_zip_code_prefix by taking min lat/lng and reporting counts. Useful to join a single coordinate per zip prefix for mapping. | Use for: Mapping customers or sellers by zip code prefix; Enriching customer/seller rows with representative coordinates
